expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: No. A non-empty revenue table only catches total pipeline failure; it will pass when every join misses

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: revenue is silently converted to zero; No blanket zeroing: preserve `NULL` as 'unknown/broken'

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: Reconciliation: compare dashboard revenue with an independent source of truth (billing/ledger)

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: Add controls that fail closed before `COALESCE` masks the problem—timing before masking, benefit of preventing silent failure

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: Schema contract: assert the upstream column exists, has the expected type, and alert on added/removed/renamed fields

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: Specific SQL with joined_rows > 0, match rate >= 0.99, null check; freshness and volume checks

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Alert routing and ownership: page or notify the data owner when these checks fail—don't rely on someone noticing a chart

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: Does not explain the danger or contrast; assumes failure is preferable but doesn't articulate why
